name: X1/X2 Student visa

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an admission letter from a recognised Chinese educational institution and a JW201 or JW202 form issued by that institution, for a program of study exceeding 180 days.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission and the required JW201/JW202 form from a recognised Chinese institution.

requirements.blocker_text: Holders must register with the local Public Security Bureau (PSB) within 30 days of arrival and apply for a Temporary/Residence Permit for Study to convert the entry visa into a long-term status.
requirements.fix_path: Complete PSB registration within 30 days of arrival.

requirement_groups.name: X2: study of 180 days or fewer

requirements.blocker_text: Requires an admission letter and JW201/JW202 form for a short-term program of 180 days or fewer; for medical programmes, an additional Internship Admission Notice is required.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission and the required documentation from a recognised Chinese institution for the short-term program.

evidence_required.document: Admission letter and JW201 or JW202 form from the Chinese institution
Passport valid at least 6 months with blank pages
PSB registration within 30 days of arrival (X1 track)

outcome.duration_length: X1: up to 5 years multiple-entry, tied to program length; X2: single-entry, up to 6 months

sources.title: China Neighbor -- China Visa Types: Complete Guide for Foreigners (2026), describing the X1/X2 distinction, PSB registration requirement, and JW201/JW202 documentation

notes: HONEST SOURCING GAP: as with cn_l_visa_visafree, this route rests on a well cross-referenced tier-3 guide rather than a directly fetched nia.gov.cn or Ministry of Education page -- the specific X1/X2 category pages were not isolated and fetched in this research pass. work_rights is 'none' as the verified default; unlike Poland's uncapped student work rights or Korea's narrow permitted-activity exceptions, no source checked in this pass documented any legal part-time work allowance for X-visa holders in China, and several general work-visa guides note that even Chinese permanent residents face province-specific work restrictions, suggesting China's system is generally more restrictive on foreign student work than the other countries in this dataset -- flagged as the verified position rather than an assumption of restrictiveness. Standard graduation pathway mirrors Korea's: X1 holders typically transition to a Z visa (work visa) and then a Foreigner's Work Permit upon graduation and securing employment, rather than having a dedicated job-seeker status -- China has no direct equivalent to Korea's D-10 or Poland's graduate permit documented in sources checked for this build.
